raw_response:
I'm seventy this year. I've been working this land since I was a boy — my father taught me, and his father taught him. I only went to primary school for a few years, but I know my fields. I have 16.9 mu, all wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone in our village. It's just me, my wife, and my grandson at home now. My son is in Shijiazhuang working construction, and he sends a little money sometimes, but I never count on it for the farm. We are smallholders — every yuan matters, and my back isn't what it used to be, so I try not to waste trips to the field.

For wheat, I always plant around National Day, usually October 3rd or 4th, after the autumn rain softens the soil. I save my own seed — I cleaned about 200 jin from last year's harvest and treated it with that red powder. Why buy seed when my own grows fine? I hire Old Zhang's tractor to rotary-till the field after the maize comes off; costs me about 50 yuan per mu. Before planting, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that's 50 jin. Then in early March, when the wheat turns green, I walk the field and if it looks a bit yellow I spread another 30 jin of urea. Last year I tried to save money on fertilizer and my yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. Never again. I'd rather borrow a bit than risk going hungry. I irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain-filling. The electricity for the pump is expensive, but what can you do? I spray herbicide once after planting. We do everything ourselves — me, my wife, and the boy. I expect about 800 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

For maize, there's no time to rest. We harvest wheat in early June and plant maize within two or three days. The window is tight — sometimes we plant while the wheat stubble is still warm. I don't plow, just open furrows with the small tiller and drop the seeds. Maize must be hybrid seed, everyone knows saved seed won't breed true. I buy it from the shop for about 45 yuan per mu. I put all the fertilizer down at planting — half a bag of compound and 30 jin of urea in the same furrow. I'm too old to make a second trip for topdressing, and the maize season is short. If the summer rains are good I might not irrigate at all, but usually I pump once at flowering, just to be safe. I spray herbicide when I plant, and I keep one packet of insecticide in the shed in case the armyworms come like they did in the east village two years ago. Harvest is late September. Should get about 850 to 900 jin per mu.

All together — seeds, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, tractor hire, and medicine — I figure I'll spend about 7,600 yuan this year. That's a lot of money for us. I don't hire labor; family labor is all we have, though it gets harder every year.
